technical.prompt: What is net operating income for a property?
expectedPoints: Property revenue minus property operating expenses
Before interest, income taxes, depreciation and capital spending
The main measure of a property's income
The basis for cap rate valuation

choices.answer: Property revenue minus property operating expenses
distractors: Rent collected minus all capital spending

technical.prompt: What is a capitalisation rate?
expectedPoints: Net operating income divided by property value
An unlevered yield on the property
Lower cap rates mean higher values for the same income
Reflects risk, growth and interest rates

choices.answer: Net operating income divided by property value

technical.prompt: What is a real estate investment trust?
expectedPoints: A company that owns or finances income-producing real estate
Avoids most corporate income tax if it meets rules
Must distribute most of its taxable income as dividends
Must hold mainly real estate assets and income

choices.answer: A tax-advantaged property company that must pay out most income
distractors: A bank that lends only for home purchases
A government agency that builds housing

technical.prompt: What are funds from operations?

The standard earnings measure for REITs

choices.answer: Net income plus property depreciation, less sale gains
distractors: Revenue minus property operating expenses only
Cash held in the bank at the end of the year
Dividends paid plus shares bought back

technical.prompt: Why do REITs report funds from operations rather than relying on net income?

FFO gives a better view of recurring earnings

choices.answer: Depreciation can understate the earnings of long-lived property
distractors: Net income is not reported by REITs
FFO is required for tax filings

technical.prompt: What are the main property types a real estate coverage group follows?
